title: The rock cycle
examples: How do the three types of rock connect in the cycle?
What process turns one rock type into another?
Can you show me an example of each rock type?

explain.say: Today we will learn about the rock cycle. It shows how rocks change over time. We will look at three main types of rock.

items: Sedimentary: form from layers of sediment
Metamorphic: change due to heat and pressure

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the rock cycle. Look at the magma, the igneous rock and the sediment. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Igneous rocks form when magma cools down. Magma is molten rock found deep underground. When it cools, it solidifies into hard rock.
Sedimentary rocks form from layers of sediment. Sediment comes from weathered bits of other rocks. These bits are then pressed together over time.
Metamorphic rocks change due to intense heat and pressure. This changes the existing rock without melting it. Think of it like changing its structure.
One rock type can become another through the cycle. For example, an existing rock can be buried and melted. When it cools, it forms a new igneous rock.

items: Sedimentary Rock → Melting → Magma → Igneous Rock
Metamorphic Rock → Melting → Magma → Igneous Rock

explain.say: In real life, the Grand Canyon shows this cycle. Layers of sedimentary rock were uplifted by forces deep in Earth's past.

faq.q: How does the cycle actually start?
faq.a: The cycle can start with any rock type. Weathering exposes the rocks to the forces that begin the cycle.
asks: Does one rock type always start the process?

faq.q: Is weathering the same as erosion?
faq.a: No, weathering is the breaking down of rock in place. Erosion is the movement of that broken-down material away from the rock.
asks: What is the difference between weathering and erosion?
Does breaking rock apart count as erosion?

faq.a: Magma is molten rock found beneath the Earth's surface. Lava is the same material once it has reached the surface.
asks: Is lava the same as magma?

faq.q: Does pressure only affect metamorphic rocks?
faq.a: Pressure is a key factor in forming metamorphic rocks. It squeezes the minerals together, changing their structure.

faq.q: How long does the whole cycle take?
faq.a: The rock cycle takes millions of years to complete. It is a very slow process happening over vast amounts of time.
asks: Is the rock cycle fast or slow?
How many years does it take for rocks to change?

facts: Igneous rocks form from cooled magma or lava.
Sedimentary rocks are formed from cemented layers of sediment.
Metamorphic rocks are changed by intense heat and pressure.
Weathering breaks down rocks on the Earth's surface.

quiz.say: Which rock type forms directly from cooling magma?
quiz.why: Igneous rocks are defined by their formation from cooled molten material.

wrong.1: Sedimentary rocks need layers of sediment to form, not just cooling.
wrong.2: Metamorphic rocks need heat and pressure, not just cooling.
wrong.3: Each rock type requires a different primary process to form.

quiz.say: If a rock is squeezed by deep earth forces, it is likely to become:
quiz.why: Squeezing and intense heat are the defining characteristics of metamorphic change.

wrong.0: Igneous rocks form from cooling magma, not just squeezing.
wrong.1: Sedimentary rocks form from deposited layers, not just pressure.
wrong.2: Weathered rock is just the starting material, not the final rock type.

quiz.say: When does the cycle show a rock turning into magma?

options.show: When the rock is buried deep enough to melt
options.say: When the rock is buried deep enough to melt

quiz.why: Melting is the process that turns any existing rock type back into magma, restarting the cycle.

wrong.1: Erosion only moves rock material away from its location.
wrong.2: Cementation only glues together loose sediments into sedimentary rock.
wrong.3: Cooling happens after magma forms, it is not the process that creates magma.
